Third development release of 0.19.0: floor plans grow into a full building tool (rooms, areas, walls and doors, cable routes with lengths, aligned floors drawn as one building in 3D, a site map base layer under each floor's drawing, device 3D models and a PDF report of a view, room or building), device profiles that hand a device its application groups, tags and fields in one step, a compliance rule builder, application flow requirements that keep flows in step on their own, intended VMs for provisioning, new routing and interface fields, a much faster dashboard and device page, and a batch of security and correctness fixes.

> [!CAUTION]
> **This is a development release. It is not stable and it contains bugs.** Do not run it in production or on data you can't restore. Take a backup before upgrading a test install, and expect behaviour to change before 0.19.0. If you run into a problem, please [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.19.0 right.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - **API tokens are capped per user.** One user may hold `API_MAX_TOKENS_PER_USER` (default 25) unexpired tokens; creating one more answers 400 until one is revoked or expires. The large-page slots are now shared across all of a user's tokens instead of one set per token.
> - **Foreign ids are refused on writes.** An id on a writable relation that is unknown or belongs to another tenant is now a 400 field error everywhere. Interface bulk add and bulk update resolve tag ids the same way and never create a tag from a name.
> - **SSH host keys can't be edited.** `PUT` and `PATCH` on a host key answer 405, and the device is fixed after upload.
> - **BGP address families have their own rows.** Per-address-family settings live on sessions and peer groups. The old `address_families` list stays as a view kept in step with them; existing lists are backfilled.
> - **Floor plans belong to a site.** Every plan and stack names a site (backfilled); the location is optional, and a plan without one covers the whole site.
> - **Site roles gain the new types.** Existing site viewer and editor roles are upgraded to cover device profiles, rooms, location types, floor plan areas, walls and cable routes, policy rules and the other new rows.
> - **New demo seeders, opt-in.** `make seed-floorplan-demo TENANT=<slug>` and `make seed-building-demo TENANT=<slug>` add an example floor plan and an example building to one tenant. Nothing is seeded on upgrade.

### Floor plans

- **Rooms.** Locations hold rooms; devices, racks and cabinets can name their room. Rooms have their own list and page with a Floor plan tab.
- **Floors and buildings.** Plans group into stacks of floors with a floor switcher. Floors can be aligned into one building: basements, a shared footprint, slab thickness and computed elevations. A level picker shows All, Up to or Only a level, with onion skin in 2D and the building drawn floor by floor in 3D. **Use same plane** on Add floor copies the outline, walls and background.
- **Site-wide plans and the Site map.** A plan can cover a whole site. New floor plan from the Site map view, location types and building outlines on the site map, and a base map layer shared by all levels above ground, with each floor's own drawing (CAD or image) on top. Basements have no map. The map frame can be moved, resized and refreshed from the Background menu; satellite maps stay in colour; plans can be up to 2,048 cells a side.
- **Areas, labels and structure.** Areas with types, colours and patterns; labels; walls, doors, trays and raised floors drawn and edited on the plan. Walls added around an area stay linked to it: moving the area moves the walls, reshaping it offers **Update walls**, and editing a linked wall offers **Update area**. **Detect outline** traces walls from the map, picture or drawing.
- **Placing objects.** Place devices, racks and cabinets from a picker with room checks, photos and save-conflict handling; free placement off the grid; devices sized by their measured dimensions.
- **Cables.** Cable routes per plan with computed lengths and tenant length rules, routed along trays, re-routed when tiles or trays move, drawn in lanes and bundles coloured from data, named along their runs, and picked one at a time where several meet. **Connect to** plans new cables between placed objects; risers carry cables between floors.
- **Reading crowded plans.** Readable object size (the default), icons on tiles when zoomed out, icon clusters that spread on hover, and callout boxes with leader lines naming tiles too small to label, with icons on or off.
- **3D.** An architectural look in both themes, uploaded GLB models for device types and devices with ports mapped onto them, floor-placed devices, navigation from the point under the cursor, and names that stay on large plans.
- **Panels and snapshots.** Detail panels for objects and cables with layouts set per device type, role, profile or tenant under Settings → Floor plans. Snapshots copy a room, location or area as a cropped copy or a live view.
- **Export.** One Export menu: the view on screen, a room or area, a floor or a whole building as PDF, with a report of the cable schedule, inventory and ports. The cable schedule PDF carries the background, the CAD drawing and close-ups round clusters of cable ends.
- **Touch.** Pinch to zoom.

### Devices, VMs and applications

- **Device profiles.** A profile hands a device or VM its application groups, tags, platform and blank custom fields in one assignment, releases them on unassign and hands items over between profiles. Profiles have a list, page and editor, and show on device and VM pages.
- **Intended VMs.** A VM can be marked intended, represent a device and carry a build; VM interfaces gain index, model and bridge, and a virtual disk API arrives. **Provision** sends an intended VM to an automation target under its own permission, and virtualization sync never overwrites, deletes or prunes an intended VM.
- **Application flow requirements.** An application states the flows it needs, with ends on its own hosts or another application's. Danbyte documents them as generated flows and keeps them in step with installs, addresses, hosts and services. Change-log entries gain a cause.
- **Custom end-of-life products.** A tenant can add its own products next to the catalog, with a Custom badge in the product picker.
- **Bulk edit** for virtual machines and platforms, with safe bulk delete for platforms.
- **Tasks** can be added from an object's Tasks tab and from the calendar.

### Networking

- **WireGuard** fields on tunnel terminations.
- **LAG bond mode,** hash policy and miimon on LAG interfaces.
- **Policy routing:** ip rule rows per device or VM, a kernel table on static routes and an out interface on NAT rules.
- **EVPN:** a DF preference per Ethernet segment member.
- **BGP:** per-address-family settings on sessions and peer groups.
- **VXLAN:** an interface type and a VTEP link on L2VPN memberships.

### Compliance, PRTG and DNS

- **Compliance rule builder.** Rules are built from object types, a scope and must-match conditions compiled to SQL, with counts per type as you build and a Results tab per type.
- **PRTG review queue** hides applied and dismissed rows by default, with a state filter and counts.
- **DNS records to IPAM in bulk.** Tick records and use **Add N to IPAM**, or **Add all to IPAM** for every record the filters show; `import_unmatched` also takes a list of ids.

### Performance

- **Dashboard** charts read the rollups and only for the widgets on show: about 9.5 s down to 0.4 s on a busy install.
- **Device and VM pages** draw at once from the list's row and fill in as the detail loads, with the tab counts in the same read.
- #455 - A device or VM page counts its addresses in one query.
- #460 - The SLA agreement list prefetches its channels.

### Fixed

- #447 - Fixes list pages that a token client read only part of.
- #448 - Fixes VRF, VLAN, route target and L2VPN counts including rows the reader can't view.
- #449 - Fixes parallel two-factor guesses all passing the limit; the attempt is counted before the code is checked.
- #453 - Fixes floor plan tile links, site map rows, detached flow names and coverage titles naming objects a site-scoped reader may not view.
- #456 - Fixes interface bulk add and bulk update accepting tag ids from another tenant.
- #457 - Fixes each new API token bringing its own large-page slots.
- #458 - Fixes SSH host keys being movable to another device after upload.
- #459 - Fixes PRTG and Zabbix error text that could include the API key.
- #461 - Fixes unlabelled controls for screen readers; a test now fails on new ones.
- #462 - Updates vulnerable frontend development dependencies.
- #463 - Fixes Windows DHCP sync failing on long client ids; a bad row is now skipped instead of stopping the run.
- **The API schema** could be served from a cache filled before the permission check. It is now cached after it.
- **Writable relations** on some endpoints accepted ids from another tenant.
- **Floor plan cables** showed to readers who could not view them.
- **VM custom fields** were not validated on a single save.
